questions.question: Why is the viewport meta tag required for responsive CSS?
questions.answer: Without it mobile browsers use a virtual desktop width and scale the page down, so media queries see a wide viewport. width=device-width, initial-scale=1 makes CSS pixels match the device width.

questions.question: What does mobile-first mean in practice?
questions.answer: Write base styles for small screens, then add enhancements with min-width media queries. This keeps base CSS simple, avoids overrides, and progressively adds complexity for larger viewports.

questions.question: How do container queries differ from media queries?
questions.answer: Media queries respond to the viewport/device features. Container queries respond to the size of a designated ancestor container, letting the same component adapt in different layout slots regardless of viewport.

questions.question: How does clamp() reduce breakpoint count?
questions.answer: clamp(min, preferred, max) scales a value fluidly between bounds, so font sizes and spacing adjust continuously instead of jumping at breakpoints. Fewer media queries are needed for type and spacing.

questions.question: What should you test beyond resizing the window?
questions.answer: Test 200% zoom and text-only zoom, long words/titles, missing images, landscape orientation, real devices, print, prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-color-scheme, and forced-colors mode.

questions.question: Make a card grid 1 column on mobile, 2 at 640px, 3 at 1024px.
Why can min-width and max-width media queries conflict at the same breakpoint?
questions.answer: Both conditions can be true at exactly that width (e.g. min-width:768px and max-width:768px), so later rules unexpectedly override. Use disjoint ranges or stick to min-width mobile-first queries.

questions.question: Why do container queries fail on a component with no container ancestor?
questions.answer: Container queries only respond to an ancestor with container-type set. Without that containment context, the query has no size to evaluate and the rules do not apply.
